https://www.grandprix.com/news/honda-tar.text: Fernando Alonso © Aston Martin Formula One Team The Japanese manufacturer endured a disastrous start to its new works partnership with Aston Martin, but confidence has risen after the team's heavily revised B-spec chassis showed signs of progress before the summer break. Honda will now add its own contribution at Zandvoort, where an upgraded power unit will debut. I think that while we won't have the best engine by the beginning of 2027, we will be getting closer to our main competitor, Honda F1 chief engineer Shintaro Orihara told f1-insider.com. We will continue to work hard to have the strongest engine by mid-2027, or at the latest by 2028. Orihara says the focus is not simply on outright power, but on making the Honda package work more effectively with Aston Martin's developing chassis. After the summer break, we want to be right back at the front with our engine, he continued. We are in close talks with Aston Martin to better integrate our power unit into their new chassis. That follows Aston Martin's substantial pre-break upgrade package, which included 11 changes and represented the first significant step away from the deeply disappointing launch specification. (GMM) Grandprix.com context: Earlier in August, Honda said its relationship with Aston Martin had improved sharply ahead of Zandvoort . Photograph: Anoush Abrar View image in fullscreen Jeremy Thomas was the acclaimed producer behind a string of commercial and critical hits. Photograph: Anoush Abrar Film industry Jeremy Thomas, British producer of The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, dies aged 77 Thomas was noted for collaborations with directors including Bernardo Bertolucci and David Cronenberg Andrew Pulver Sat 12 Sep 2026 10.01 EDT Last modified on Sat 12 Sep 2026 10.19 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Jeremy Thomas, the distinguished British producer of films including Sexy Beast, High-Rise and the multi-Oscar-winning The Last Emperor, has died aged 77. A representative for Thomas said he died on Friday “peacefully, at his country home in Oxfordshire, surrounded by his family and loved ones”. Thomas, who started producing feature films in the early 1970s, was known for forging strong creative relationships with acclaimed auteurs, producing a string of films directed by the likes of Nicolas Roeg, David Cronenberg and Bernardo Bertolucci . Jeremy Thomas: producer was cross between a kindly Cambridge don and the movie world’s cool uncle Read more The Last Emperor, directed by Bertolucci, was an early triumph for Thomas, winning nine Oscars including best picture. He went on to become a major figure in the British film-making establishment, including a spell as chair of the British Film Institute and winning a Bafta for outstanding British contribution to cinema. Born in 1949, Thomas’s father, Ralph, was a prolific film director whose work included the popular Doctor in the House series starring Dirk Bogarde, and his uncle Gerald Thomas directed all 30 of the Carry On films. Thomas started out as an assistant editor, working on the Jimmy Cliff thriller The Harder They Come and Ken Loach’s Family Life, before gaining his first producer credit on Mad Dog Morgan in 1976, with Dennis Hopper as the 19th-century Australian outlaw of the title. Thomas was quickly into his stride, making Bad Timing, Significance and Eureka with Roeg, The Shout with Jerzy Skolimowski and Merry Christmas, Mr Lawrence with the Japanese master director Nagisa Oshima. The success of The Last Emperor, which Thomas had to finance independently, consolidated his status as a leading figure in British cinema, and he subsequently concentrated on prestige projects including The Sheltering Sky and Little Buddha (both with Bertolucci) and Naked Lunch (with Cronenberg). Thomas then suggested to Cronenberg he should direct JG Ballard’s Crash, and the resulting film was enormously controversial , resulting in local authority bans in several areas in the UK. Following this, Thomas’s films included riskier propositions, such as Sexy Beast, directed by Jonathan Glazer, an adaptation of Alexander Trocchi’s Young Adam, by David Mackenzie, and Terry Gilliam’s bizarre corpse comedy Tideland. Later highlights were Jim Jarmusch’s vampire fantasy Only Lovers Left Alive, another Ballard adaptation, High-Rise, directed by Ben Wheatley, and Tale of Tales and Dogman from the Italian director Matteo Garrone. In 2019 Thomas was the subject of a documentary by Mark Cousins , who accompanied him on his car drive from the UK to the Cannes film festival for another Garrone film, Pinocchio; it screened there in 2021. Thomas also directed one film himself: All the Little Animals, starring Christian Bale, which was released in 1999. His most recent film, Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo, directed by Takashi Miike, is due to premiere at the Toronto film festival on Monday. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/16/heli.text: An NBC news television helicopter crashed into a car park in Los Angeles on Tuesday, killing at least three people.The helicopter crashed near a storage building in the neighbourhood of Chatsworth in the San Fernando Valley, as news crews were covering the bus crash that left at least two people dead and six others injured, according to the Los Angeles Fire Department. A fourth person was taken to hospital, though their condition was unknown.Colleen Williams, an NBC4 Los Angeles anchor, confirmed during a live broadcast that the station’s chopper went down just before 7 pm.“We are going to take a couple of minutes to think about that and process it,” she said, her voice shaking with emotion. Moments later, coverage was abruptly cut off.The Los Angeles Fire Department said it was still working to determine how many of the victims had been on board the aircraft.At least one person killed was on the ground outside, spokesperson Captain Branden Silverman told reporters."We're trying to determine how many patients were inside the helicopter," Silverman said.The crash occurred near the scene of a separate deadly bus accident, though the connection between the two incidents, if any, was not immediately clear.Photos and videos online showed around half of an SUV lodged into the side of an MTA bus and a large group of fire crew working around the crash.Two people were reportedly killed and six others were injured after an SUV crashed into a city bus in Los Angeles, officials said.According to the fire department, more than 50 firefighters responded to the helicopter crash. The fire had damaged four vehicles and two storage containers but was out by Tuesday evening, according to officials.Silverman described the helicopter as “pretty well destroyed” and said they’re going to have to go through the rubble to see how many victims were on board.According to media reports, the helicopter came down into a park serving a large single-storey building, striking or landing near several parked vehicles.The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration will be handling the investigation.
